reasoning: Roofline marks compute bottleneck (Compute SOL 88.4% vs Memory SOL 42.1%). Kernel metrics match this: sm throughput is 88.36% of peak sustained elapsed while DRAM throughput is only 42.12%, so performance is limited by arithmetic throughput rather than bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: High non-tensor math intensity on VALU pipelines (no tensor-core usage), especially from repeated reductions and activation math in inner loops.

evidence.interpretation: No tensor/matrix-core acceleration; work is executed on regular compute pipelines, which are already near saturation.

fixes.fix: Restructure dot-product sections (w1/w2 matmul-like parts) to use MFMA/tensor-core-friendly Triton patterns and datatypes where possible (e.g., block shapes and layouts aligned for matrix instructions).
fixes.rationale: Shifting heavy GEMV/GEMM-like operations from VALU to matrix units increases effective compute throughput and reduces pressure on saturated scalar/vector ALUs.

root_causes.cause: Very high instruction workload per dispatch from nested TOPK × INTER_DIM × MODEL_DIM loops with per-element dequant scaling and sigmoid path.

evidence.interpretation: Extremely large dynamic instruction count indicates instruction throughput pressure is a key limiter.

fixes.fix: Reduce instruction count by hoisting/reusing scales and invariant index math, and fuse gate/up computations to reuse loaded x_q/x_s and reduce duplicate operations inside k/j loops.
fixes.rationale: Lower dynamic instruction count directly relieves compute pipeline pressure in a compute-bound kernel, improving time-to-solution even without higher memory bandwidth.
